en: Rāhulabhadra:
*Prajñāpāramitāstotra* Homage to you, O immeasurable Perfection of Wisdom, who are free from conceptual construction!
You, whose every limb is entirely faultless, are gazed upon by those who are themselves irreproachable.
He who beholds you with true devotion— as stainless as space, free from conceptual proliferation, and beyond syllables— he truly beholds the Tathāgata.
O Noble Lady, the virtuous perceive no difference between you, who are rich in qualities, and the Buddha, the Teacher of the World, just as there is none between the moon and its moonlight.
O you who are compassionate and fond of devotion, those whose nature is mercy, having approached you— who are preceded by the Buddha and the Dharma— attain incomparable greatness with ease.
O you of unfailing vision, even one who beholds you according to the prescribed rite but once, when their disposition is pure,
will certainly attain accomplishment.
"O affectionate one, you are the nourisher and the mother of all heroes whose souls are devoted to the welfare of others."
Since the Buddhas, the compassionate teachers of the world, are your sons, you too,
O auspicious one, are the grandmother of all sentient beings.
O blameless one, by means of all the stainless perfections,
you are always followed, like the crescent moon by the stars.
Having approached those to be trained here and there, you alone, though manifold in form, are praised by the Tathāgatas under various names.
Just as drops of dew inevitably perish upon encountering the radiance of the sun,
so too do the faults and the arguments of disputants come to an end upon encountering you.
You alone are the source of terror for the ignorant, appearing with a fearsome aspect; yet you are the source of consolation for the wise, appearing with a serene aspect.
O Mother, how could passion and hatred exist in anyone else for one who has no attachment even toward you, his own protector? (RahPps 12)
You do not come from anywhere, nor do you go anywhere;
even in all locations, you are not perceived by the wise.
Those who do not perceive you in this way, yet take refuge in you with sincere devotion,
and having taken refuge, are liberated— this is a great marvel.
Seeing you alone, one is bound; not seeing you, one is also bound.
Seeing you alone, one is liberated; not seeing you, one is also liberated.
Oh, you are truly wonderful, O illustrious one; you are profound.
You are exceedingly difficult to comprehend; like an illusion, you are seen and yet you are not seen.
Cultivated by Buddhas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas, you are the sole path to liberation; there is no other—this is certain.
Out of compassion for embodied beings, the Lords of the World, prioritizing conventional usage for the sake of designation, speak of you and yet do not speak of you.
Who here is capable of praising you, who are causeless and stainless, who transcend the entire domain of speech, and who are not dependent on anything whatsoever? (RahPps 19)
Even though this is so, we are perfectly content, desiring to praise you—who, though beyond praise—by means of such conventional paths of speech. (RahPps 20)
Whatever merit has been accumulated by me through praising the Perfection of Wisdom, by that may the entire world swiftly become devoted to the Perfection of Wisdom. (RahPps 21)
